name: Côte d'Or

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

climate: Pinot Noir and Chardonnay sit in their sweet spot, so the wines can show the style they are known for.

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards. The Grand Crus usually sit mid-slope and higher, with the best sun and drainage.

notes: Red Burgundy is known for savory fleshiness and farmyard aromas, though modern styles lean lighter, fruitier and cleaner.
In good years, red Burgundy develops complex fruit and forest floor flavors, often peaking 15 to 20 years after the vintage.
Good white Burgundy from the Côte d'Or needs at least three years in bottle to show its aromas and character.
Grand cru wines are made for cellaring and usually need at least five to seven years.
Aligoté makes light whites with slightly herbal flavor and higher acidity than Chardonnay.

blurb.text: A Burgundy area split into the Côte de Nuits, Côte de Beaune and the two Hautes-Côtes. Pinot Noir is the most planted grape at 66%, followed by Chardonnay at 27% and Aligoté at 6%.
